title: Germs: bacteria and viruses
examples: What is the difference between a germ and a disease?
Can I get sick from touching things?
Are all bacteria bad for me?

explain.say: Today we will learn about tiny living things called germs.
Viruses are much smaller and are not truly alive.
Germs spread when we touch contaminated surfaces.
Some bacteria are helpful and keep us healthy.
In real life, washing your hands stops germ spread.

faq.q: Are viruses always dangerous to humans?
faq.a: No, some viruses are harmless or even necessary for life. For example, some viruses are needed for certain processes in nature. You might ask: What about the common cold? Or are all viruses bad?
asks: Do viruses always make you sick?

faq.q: How do I stop germs from getting into my body?
faq.a: The best way is practicing good hygiene like washing hands often. You should also cover your mouth when you cough or sneeze. You might ask: What is the best way to stay clean? Or how do I prevent infection?
asks: What is the best way to stay clean?

faq.q: Can I treat a virus with antibiotics?
faq.a: No, antibiotics only work against bacteria, not viruses. You must see a doctor for advice on treating infections. You might ask: Does medicine cure viruses? Or do antibiotics work on everything?

faq.q: What are the good bacteria in my body?
faq.a: The good bacteria live in your gut and help you digest food. They also help train your immune system to fight bad germs. You might ask: Where do good bacteria live? Or what helps my digestion?

faq.q: If I get sick, how long until I feel better?
faq.a: This depends on the germ and your body's ability to fight it off. Rest and good nutrition help your body recover faster. You might ask: How long does it take to get better? Or what helps recovery?
asks: How long does it take to get better?

facts: Bacteria are single-celled organisms that can reproduce on their own.
Viruses are much smaller than bacteria and need a living cell to reproduce.
Washing hands with soap and water is very effective at removing germs.
The gut contains many helpful bacteria that aid digestion.

quiz.say: Which type of germ is described as being much smaller than bacteria and needing a host cell?
quiz.show: Viruses need a host cell to reproduce.
quiz.why: Viruses are not truly alive and must hijack a cell to multiply.

wrong.0: Antibiotics are medicines, not types of germs.
wrong.1: Soap is a cleaning agent, not a germ type.
wrong.3: Bacteria are living cells that can reproduce on their own.

quiz.say: If you wash your hands thoroughly, what are you mainly removing?
quiz.why: Washing physically removes the pathogens from your skin.

wrong.0: While it removes dirt, the main goal is germ removal.
wrong.1: You are removing both good and bad bacteria.
wrong.2: You are removing all types of germs present.

quiz.say: Which germ type is often helpful in the digestive system?
quiz.why: Many beneficial bacteria live in the gut to help break down food.

wrong.0: Soap is a cleanser, not a biological organism.
wrong.2: Viruses are generally harmful and do not help digestion.
wrong.3: Antibiotics are treatments, not the helpful germ type.
